title: Simon Game
summary: Two-color Simon game with progressive difficulty and a Fun Mode that swaps button positions

data.text: A two-color Simon memory game built with Qt Widgets and C++17 for CS 3505 (Software Practice II) at the University of Utah. The player replays sequences of red and blue flashes that grow longer and faster with each correct round. A bonus Fun Mode swaps the button positions before each flash, forcing the player to track colors rather than positions. Solo project — 17 commits, 512 lines of code.

items.content: Designed a sequence generation and validation system using std::vector<bool> — each round appends a random color via QRandomGenerator, then plays back the full sequence with timed single-shot QTimer events
Implemented progressive difficulty — flash interval starts at 1000ms and decreases by 50ms per round (minimum 200ms), making sequences harder to follow as the game advances

Built input validation that compares each player click against the expected sequence position, advancing on match, triggering game-over on mismatch, and scheduling the next round after a 500ms delay when the full sequence is completed
Used signals to decouple model from view — the model emits sendCurrentColor, sendPlayStatus, sendGameStatus, and sendCurrentSequenceStatus without any knowledge of the UI layer
Built the button flash animation system — temporarily applies a highlight stylesheet to the target button, then reverts after 300ms using QTimer::singleShot
Added keyboard bindings (key 1 for red, key 2 for blue) as shortcuts alongside click input, with buttons disabled during sequence playback to prevent input during flashes
Implemented a progress bar that tracks the player's position within the current sequence, resetting at the start of each new round
Designed dynamic UI state management — game-over message, progress bar visibility, start/restart button text, and Fun Mode toggle all update based on game status signals
Created custom stylesheet-driven button styling with distinct normal, pressed, and flash states for red and blue buttons, structured as reusable style string constants in the header

Implemented a button-swap mechanic that removes the red and blue buttons from the QGridLayout and re-adds them in swapped columns before each flash, so the player must track color rather than position
Added timing coordination between the swap and flash — delays ensure the layout swap completes before the flash animation fires, preventing visual collisions
Built a toggle system with a Fun Mode button that switches between normal and fun modes, showing a fun.png icon when active and resetting button positions on mode change

Flash and swap timing collisions in Fun Mode: When Fun Mode swaps button positions before each flash, the swap and flash animations would fire simultaneously, causing the wrong button to light up. Solved by chaining QTimer::singleShot delays — the swap executes first, then the flash fires after a short delay, ensuring the layout settles before the visual highlight is applied.

Button positions not resetting after Fun Mode toggle: Toggling Fun Mode off mid-game left the buttons in their swapped positions. Fixed by tracking a swapped boolean and forcing a position reset in the toggle handler, restoring red to column 1 and blue to column 3 regardless of current state.

Stylesheet duplication across button states: Each button had separate normal, pressed, and flash stylesheets with repeated border-radius, font-size, and layout properties. Refactored by extracting shared style fragments into reusable QString constants in the header file, composing the final stylesheets from a base + color-specific override.
Languages: C++17
Frameworks: Qt Widgets, QTimer, QRandomGenerator, QGridLayout, QProgressBar, QShortcut
Patterns: Model-View separation, Observer pattern (Qt signals/slots), event-driven game loop with single-shot timers
Concepts: Timed sequence playback with progressive speedup, dynamic layout manipulation (runtime widget reparenting), stylesheet-based visual state management, keyboard shortcut binding
Tools: Git, QMake, Qt Designer (.ui), Qt Resource System (.qrc)
